latin: चणकस्य समान् खण्डान् कल्पयित्वा विचक्षणः । निशाजीरकतीक्ष्णाद्यैः शुण्ठीधान्यकहिङ्गुभिः ॥ ४९ ॥ चूर्णितैर्मेलयित्वा तांस्तप्ततैले विनिक्षिपेत् । समानार्द्रकखण्डांश्च चणकान् हरितानपि ॥ १४५० ॥ श्लक्ष्णमांसैः क्षिपेत्कोलं निष्पावान् कोमलानपि । पलाण्डुशकलान् वापि लशुनं वापि निक्षिपेत् ॥ ५१ ॥ एवं पूर्वोदितं सूदः प्रयुञ्जीत यथारुचि । शोषितेऽम्लरसे पश्चात्सिद्धमुत्तार्य धूपयेत् ॥ ५२ ॥
english: Having made pieces [of meat] the size of a chickpea, the discerning cook should mix them with *niśā* [turmeric], cumin, *tīkṣṇa* [a pungent spice; the nighaṇṭus give the name to both black pepper and mustard] and the rest, and with dried ginger, coriander, and asafoetida, all reduced to powder, and throw them into heated oil — and pieces of fresh ginger cut to the same size, and green chickpeas too. Along with the finely cut meats he should put in *kola* [either the middle grade of jujube in the Ayurvedic *badara* triad, or black pepper: Monier-Williams gives both senses, and the *Rāja-nighaṇṭu* lists *kola* among the synonyms of *Piper*] and tender *niṣpāva* pods [lablab or hyacinth bean, *Lablab purpureus*, whose pods are eaten whole while tender]; or else he may put in slices of onion, or garlic. In this way the cook should apply, as he likes, the [sauce] described earlier [*pūrvoditaṃ* is neuter singular, agreeing with the *pralehaka* of 1446 — the sour sauce of the previous recipe, not a method]. Afterwards, when the sour juice has dried away, he should take the finished dish off the fire and perfume it with aromatic smoke.

latin: बदराकारकान् खण्डान् पूर्ववच्चूर्णमिश्रितान् । आर्द्रकांस्तत्प्रमाणांश्च पक्वतैले विपाचयेत् ॥ ५३ ॥ वार्ताकशकलांश्चैव मूलकस्य च खण्डकान् । पलाण्ड्वार्द्रकसम्भूतान् मुद्गाङ्कुरविनिर्मितान् ॥ ५४ ॥ वटकान् निक्षिपेत्तत्र मेषकस्य च चूर्णकम् । कासमर्देन संयुक्तं पलान्यन्यानि कानिचित् ॥ ५५ ॥ सुसिद्धं वासयेद्धूपैर्नानारसविमिश्रितम् । नानाद्रव्यसमेता सा कवचन्दी भवेच्छुभा ॥ ५६ ॥
english: Pieces [of meat] shaped like jujubes, mixed with the powders as before, and pieces of fresh ginger of that same measure: these he should cook through in well-heated oil. And slices of eggplant, and pieces of radish, and — made up of onion and fresh ginger, formed out of mung sprouts — *vaṭakas*: these he should put in there, and powder of *meṣaka* [thus the print here; at 1459 and 1467 the edition prints *methaka*, fenugreek, and the compound *methaka-cūrṇaka* at 1459 is identical to this one, so the same word is probably meant, but Shrigondekar does not emend], combined with *kāsamarda* [*Senna occidentalis*, whose leaves are used as a pot-herb], and some other meats. When it is well cooked and mixed with the various juices, he should perfume it with aromatic smokes. Endowed with many substances, that *kavacandī* will be excellent.

latin: स्थूलामलकसङ्काशान् शुद्धमांसस्य खण्डकान् । काथयेद्राजिकातोयैर्नागरार्द्रकसंयुतैः ॥ ५७ ॥ स्थापयेत्तज्जलं पात्रे रिक्ते चाम्लैर्विपाचयेत् । तत्समान् शुण्ठकान् क्षिप्त्वा सैन्धवं तत्र योजयेत् ॥ ५८ ॥ मेथकचूर्णकं तत्र धान्याकस्य च पूलिकाम् । निक्षिप्योत्तारयेत्सूदो घृतं वान्यत्र तापयेत् ॥ ५९ ॥ सुतप्ते च घृते पश्चाल्लशुनं हिङ्गुना सह । प्रक्षिप्य संस्कृतं मांसं तस्यां स्थाल्यां प्रवेशयेत् ॥ १४६० ॥ पिहितं च ततः कुर्यात्किञ्चित्कालं प्रतीक्ष्य च । उत्तारयेत्ततः सिद्धं पुर्यलाख्यमिदं वरम् ॥ ६१ ॥
english: Pieces of clean meat resembling large *āmalakas* he should boil in mustard-water combined with dried ginger and fresh ginger. He should set that liquid aside in an empty vessel and cook it with sour things. Having thrown in *śuṇṭhakas* of that same size, he should add rock salt to it, and having put in fenugreek powder and a small bundle of coriander, the cook should take it off the fire; and he should heat ghee elsewhere. Afterwards, when the ghee is thoroughly hot, having thrown garlic into it together with asafoetida, he should put the prepared meat into that pot. Then he should cover it, and after waiting a little while, take it off the fire when done. This excellent [dish] is called *puryala*.

latin: पृष्ठवंशसमुद्भूतं शुद्धं मांसं प्रगृह्यते । घनसारप्रमाणानि कृत्वा खण्डानि मूलकैः ॥ ६२ ॥ विध्वा तु बहुशस्तानि बहुरन्ध्राणि कारयेत् । हिङ्ग्वार्द्रकरसंयुक्तं सैन्धवेन च पेषयेत् ॥ ६३ ॥ शूलप्रोतानि कृत्वा तान्यङ्गारेषु प्रतापयेत् । घृतेन सिञ्चेत्पाकज्ञो वारंवारं विवर्तयेत् ॥ ६४ ॥ सिद्धेषु मारिचं चूर्णं विकिरेत्सैन्धवान्वितम् । नाम्ना भडित्रकं रुच्यं लघु पथ्यं मनोहरम् ॥ ६५ ॥
english: Clean meat that comes from beside the backbone is taken. Having made pieces of the measure of *ghanasāra* [camphor — a lexical synonym; manuscript A here reads *karpūra*, the chapter's own word for camphor, outright] with *mūlakas* [the printed reading is *mūḷakaiḥ*, instrumental plural of *mūlaka*, radish, manuscript D reading *pūḷakaiḥ*; construed with *vidhvā* in the next line the sense required is a piercing tool, which no attested sense of *mūlaka* supplies, so the reading is probably corrupt], he should pierce them many times over and make them full of holes. And he should pound the meat, combined with the juices of asafoetida and fresh ginger, together with rock salt. Having threaded them on skewers, he should roast them over the embers; one who knows cooking should baste them with ghee and turn them over again and again. When they are done, he should scatter pepper powder mixed with rock salt over them. By name this is *bhaḍitraka*: appetizing, light, wholesome, delightful.

latin: अनेनैव प्रकारेण जर्जरीकृत्य खण्डकान् । स्थाल्यामम्लेन संयोज्य पाचयेद्धिङ्गुना सह ॥ ६६ ॥ आर्द्रकस्य रसेनापि धान्यकस्य रसेन च । जीरकस्य च चूर्णेन मेथकस्य च मिश्रयेत् ॥ ६७ ॥ शोषयित्वा द्रवं सर्वं घृतेन परिभजयेत् । क्षिपेच्च मरिचं भृष्टे सूदो हुण्डभडित्रके ॥ ६८ ॥
english: Having riddled the pieces with holes in this very same way [a back-reference to the piercing at 1463], and joined them with sour liquid in a pot, he should cook them with asafoetida. He should mix in also the juice of fresh ginger and the juice of coriander, and powder of cumin, and of fenugreek. When all the liquid has dried away, he should *paribhajayet* them with ghee [so the print, which corrects the manuscripts' *parivajayet*; the sense the passage needs is 'fry them all over', which *paribharjayet* would give — and this chapter's manuscripts elsewhere lose a *repha* and confuse *va* for *bha* in exactly that way]. And when the *huṇḍa-bhaḍitraka* has fried — the *bhaḍitraka* done in a pot, *huṇḍa* being the vernacular word for a large cooking vessel, as against the skewered version above — the cook should throw pepper on it.

latin: मेषस्य कन्धरां छित्वा स्थाल्यां रक्तं विधारितम् । मर्दयेत्करशाखाभिर्निक्षिप्य लवणं मनाक् ॥ ६९ ॥ मृद्यमाने तु रुधिरे सिराजालविनिःस्रुते । अपनीय तथा शुद्धं कीलालं पिहितं न्यसेत् ॥ १४७० ॥ क्रोडदेशात्समारभ्य कर्त्रिकाग्रेण पाटिताम् । त्वचं विभज्य गात्रेभ्यो हरेद्बाह्यान्तरास्थिताम् ॥ ७१ ॥ पूर्वोद्दिष्टप्रदेशेषु स्थितं मांसमथाहरेत् । स्नायुग्रन्थिविनिर्मुक्तं खण्डशः परिकल्पयेत् ॥ ७२ ॥ पूगीफलप्रमाणानि कृत्वा खण्डानि पूर्ववत् । संस्कुर्यात्पूर्ववच्चूर्णैरम्लैश्च परिपाचयेत् ॥ ७३ ॥ स्तोकावशेषपाकेऽस्मिन्न्यस्तं रक्तं विनिक्षिपेत् । पूर्णे पाके समुत्तार्य धूपयेद्धिङ्गुजीरकैः ॥ ७४ ॥ कर्पूरचूर्णकं तस्मिन्नेलाचूर्णेन संयुतम् । विकिरेन्मरिचैर्युक्तं कृष्णपाकमिदं वरम् ॥ ७५ ॥
english: Having cut the sheep's neck, the blood being held in a pot, he should knead it with the fingers, putting in a little salt. And when the blood, under the kneading, has had the net of fibres run out of it, having taken that away, he should set down the clean *kīlāla* [blood], covered. Beginning at the chest, he should separate from the limbs the hide, split with the point of a knife, and take away what lies both outside and within. Then he should take the meat lying in the regions indicated earlier, free it of sinew and knots of gristle, and cut it into pieces. Having made the pieces of the measure of an areca nut, as before, he should season them with the powders as before and cook them thoroughly with sour things. When only a little of this cooking is left, he should throw in the blood that was set aside. When the cooking is complete, he should take it off the fire and perfume it with asafoetida and cumin. Over it he should scatter camphor powder combined with cardamom powder and with peppercorns. This excellent [dish] is *kṛṣṇapāka* [the black cooking].
